findings.name: a graceful control stop+start reuses generation 1
findings.detail: a graceful stop removes the persisted lifecycle record, so the restarted owner begins a new lifecycle at generation 1 instead of continuing the counter; a crash restart keeps the record and advances it. A stale --generation value from the previous lifecycle can therefore collide with the new one. The project declares no monotonicity requirement across a graceful stop, so the driver records this and asserts the observed rule rather than a requirement.

findings.name: A11 — the cross-device receipt is verified by reading, not by driving traffic
findings.detail: this driver exercised only the LAN address 192.168.0.3 (tailscale 100.66.1.82); the cross-device exchange was driven by the A11 unit at commit 869aff8, whose receipt the driver now verifies by reading: present, two distinct non-loopback hosts, no recorded gaps. Loopback and same-host non-loopback are never passed off as cross-device, and that exchange is not re-driven here. A finding is recorded rather than a gap because the requirement is satisfied by integrated evidence.

resolved_defects.title: agentteams control stop reported STOP_TIMEOUT while a WebUI client socket was open
resolved_defects.observed: agentteams control stop --generation 1 exited 1 with "STOP_TIMEOUT: control pid=41072 did not exit after SIGTERM"; the daemon exited ~0.25s later and the state was consistent (state=stopped, pid gone, listener port closed)
resolved_defects.root_cause: the shutdown promise awaited server.close(() => resolveClose()) with no server.closeIdleConnections()/server.closeAllConnections(); server.close() only stops accepting and waits for existing sockets, so a live keep-alive/SSE client socket held the daemon past the caller's bounded wait
resolved_defects.minimal_repro: start a registry and a control daemon, open /api/v1/events twice (read one frame, reader.cancel() each), then agentteams control stop --config control.toml --generation <n> -> exit 1, STOP_TIMEOUT after ~5.17s, pid gone ~0.25s later. Variants measured: one SSE subscription -> clean stop in 269ms; zero -> 251ms; 30 pooled plain requests -> 227ms; reader.cancel(), controller.abort() and 5 pooled requests + 1 SSE all still reproduced it
resolved_defects.impact: a correct shutdown was reported as a failure to the operator; no history was lost (A09 retention held) and agent-to-agent traffic was unaffected (A10 passed while the control daemon was down)
resolved_defects.fix: the stop path also calls server.closeIdleConnections() and server.closeAllConnections()
resolved_defects.red_test: the new case in runtime/control-process.spec.ts opens the real event stream, reads one frame, keeps the socket open and stops the daemon; it failed with STOP_TIMEOUT: control pid=<pid> did not exit after SIGTERM after 5.37s and passes now

resolved_defects.title: the control daemon's durable kind:connection history did not survive a stop
resolved_defects.observed: after a clean stop and restart, /api/v1/history?version=1&limit=50&kind=connection returned an empty page; the durable connection history the daemon declares was gone
resolved_defects.root_cause: stopControlDaemon called removeOwnedState, which deleted the daemon's whole data directory, and createControlNetworkStatus stores the history store in exactly that directory (runtime/control-process.ts:555, createAcpHistoryStore({ directory: intent.daemon.dataDirectory })), even though the code comment calls that history durable. The defect was masked because the STOP_TIMEOUT above threw before the removal, so the directory survived by accident; fixing the stop wait exposed it
resolved_defects.minimal_repro: write one real connection-history record through the real D05 owner, stop and restart the control daemon, then read the history page; it came back empty
resolved_defects.impact: every clean control stop destroyed the durable kind:connection history, which D06 acceptance requires to survive a restart ("restart 观察和 history 恢复")
resolved_defects.fix: stop now removes only the runtime ownership record and keeps the data directory, matching the agent daemon
resolved_defects.red_test: the new case in runtime/control-process.spec.ts writes one real connection-history record through the real D05 owner, stops and restarts the daemon, and asserts the page returns byte-identical; it failed with expected { records: [] } to deeply equal { records: [ ... ] } and passes now

The policy went from a driver defect (single attempt, three aborted runs at 2026-10-11 21:06/21:12 and 2026-10-12 05:05) to d8f5cd1 (six attempts, fresh request id per attempt, backoff 30s/60s/120s/240s/480s, only 5xx-shaped refusals retried), then d05f3a0 (the second observed upstream shape, turn failed: Connection error, classified as transient; a frame timeout retried only while the engine is still alive, so a dead engine still fails fast). At 2026-10-12 07:56 the pool refused twice and served attempt 3: the run that would previously have died at A02 passed it. A deterministic failure is never retried, and exhaustion records a gap rather than a fabricated pass.

closed_gaps.earlier_reason: this driver runs on one physical host (LAN 192.168.0.3) and cannot itself produce a cross-device receipt; loopback and same-host non-loopback are never passed off as cross-device.
